record.original_question: For the semi-equational conditional term-rewriting system that linearizes Combinatory Logic extended with surjective pairing, with rules I x -> x, K x y -> x, S x y z -> (x z)(y z), D1(D x y) -> x, D2(D x y) -> y, and conditional rules from convertibility to D(D1 x)(D2 y) -> x and D(D1 x)(D2 y) -> y, is the system confluent? If it is confluent, does it have an effective normal-form strategy?

evidence.quote: Is a certain conditional rewrite system, which is a linearization of Combinatory Logic extended with surjective pairing, confluent?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the first-order conditional term-rewriting system R over the signature consisting of constants I, K, S, D, unary symbols D1 and D2, and a binary application operator (written by juxtaposition, left-associative). The unconditional rewrite rules of R are:

  (I)  I x  -> x,
  (K)  K x y -> x,
  (S)  S x y z -> (x z)(y z),
  (P1) D1 (D x y) -> x,
  (P2) D2 (D x y) -> y.

In addition, R has two semi-equational conditional rules using the convertibility (i.e., symmetric-transitive closure of one-step rewriting) relation =_R generated by R itself:

  (C1)  D (D1 z) (D2 w) -> z   if   z =_R w,
  (C2)  D (D1 z) (D2 w) -> w   if   z =_R w.

(This system is the "surjective-pairing linearization" of Combinatory Logic extended with surjective pairing: the nonlinear identity D(D1 t)(D2 t) = t is replaced by the conditional rules (C1) and (C2).)

Questions:
(a) Is R confluent, i.e., does t ->>_R u and t ->>_R v imply that there exists w with u ->>_R w and v ->>_R w?
(b) If R is confluent, does it admit an effective normal-form strategy — that is, a computable function F on terms such that for every term t, F(t) is a one-step R-rewrite reduct of t whenever t is not in R-normal form, and iterating F from t terminates at an R-normal form whenever t has any R-normal form?
artifact.status_search_result: A closely related problem — confluence of an extension of Combinatory Logic by Boolean constants (RTA open problem 15, "CL-pc") — was solved by Ł. Czajka (FSCD 2017, arXiv:1306.2069) with a Coq-formalized confluence proof. However, the specific semi-equational conditional rewrite system linearizing Combinatory Logic extended with surjective pairing (with rules D1(D x y)->x, D2(D x y)->y, and the conditional pair-elimination rules) is a distinct system, and the search did not surface a definitive proof or refutation of its confluence, nor an effective normal-form strategy result. Klop–de Vrijer's broader investigations of CL/λ with surjective pairing show such systems are notoriously delicate, and the related question about untyped λ + surjective pairing failing Church–Rosser is well known. Current status of this precise question is not clearly established by available sources.

status_evidence.title: Confluence of an Extension of Combinatory Logic by Boolean Constants
status_evidence.snippet: Solves RTA open problem 15: confluence of CL-pc, a conditional rewriting extension of Combinatory Logic by Boolean constants.
status_evidence.claim: A related but distinct open problem on conditional CL extensions has been solved; this does not directly resolve the surjective-pairing linearization question.

status_evidence.title: Extending the Extensional Lambda Calculus with Surjective Pairing is Conservative
status_evidence.snippet: Støvring (2006) shows λβη+SP is a conservative extension of λβη, addressing an old Klop–de Vrijer question, while noting that the standard reduction relation for λβηSP is not confluent.
status_evidence.claim: Background on the difficulty of confluence for surjective-pairing extensions.

status_evidence.title: Unique Normal Forms for Lambda Calculus with Surjective Pairing (Klop, de Vrijer)
status_evidence.snippet: Klop and de Vrijer study unique-normal-form properties of λ with surjective pairing using conditional-linearization techniques.
status_evidence.claim: Conditional linearizations of surjective pairing have been studied; confluence of the linearized system is the natural further question.
